title: Advanced Machine Learning
lead: A structured route through the methods, models, and worked calculations in Advanced Machine Learning.

title: Machine learning foundations and learning paradigms
lead: Machine learning is useful when examples can teach a system a pattern that is hard to specify by hand. This page connects the learning problem, its data and performance goal, and the main ways a learner can receive feedback.

title: Classifier boundaries and decision-tree representations
lead: How the model’s representation shapes the boundaries and regions it can learn, illustrated with Spam/Ham email examples.

title: Evaluation, generalization and model choice
lead: How to judge a learner, choose an appropriate model, and interpret what a score can and cannot tell us about new cases.

title: Supervised Learning: Evaluation, kNN, and Decision Trees
lead: How labeled examples support prediction, how to evaluate fairly, and how nearest neighbors and decision trees turn examples into classifications.

title: Naive Bayes Classification (Supplemental Lecture Material)
lead: A compact probabilistic classifier that combines class priors with feature likelihoods under a class-conditional independence assumption.

title: Support vector machines, margins and kernels (supplemental)
lead: A maximum-margin linear classifier, extended to tolerate violations and form nonlinear boundaries through feature maps and kernels.

title: Unsupervised Learning: Clustering and Evaluation
lead: Learn how clustering discovers structure without target labels, how k-means and hierarchical methods form groups, and how to judge whether the resulting clusters are useful.

title: Neural Computation and Perceptron Learning
lead: How a weighted neuron becomes a classifier, how the perceptron adjusts its boundary, and why XOR needs a richer representation.

title: Multilayer Networks, Gradient Descent, and Training Practice
lead: How multilayer networks combine affine layers and activations, and how gradients, objectives, and training schedules shape their learning.

title: Least Mean Squares and the Delta Rule
lead: LMS adjusts a linear filter by following the instantaneous squared-error gradient.

title: Backpropagation: Derivation and Layerwise Updates
lead: Backpropagation applies the chain rule to assign loss gradients to every MLP weight and bias.

title: Dimensionality Reduction, Feature Selection, and MDS
lead: Reduce feature width while deciding which geometry or task information the smaller representation should preserve.

title: Principal Component Analysis
lead: PCA finds orthogonal linear directions that retain the greatest variance, then projects observations into a smaller coordinate system.

title: FastMap and Random Projection
lead: Two ways to reduce dimensions: recursively embed pairwise distances with FastMap, or multiply vectors by a low-dimensional random map with probabilistic distance guarantees.

title: Transfer Learning, Multitask Learning, and Fine-Tuning
lead: Reuse learned representations across related tasks and domains, then choose carefully which target parameters to adapt.

title: Domain Adaptation, Shift, and Negative Transfer
lead: Compare what transfers across domains, what labels remain available, and when transferred knowledge can hurt.

title: Deep Learning Foundations and Regularization
lead: How neural networks learn representations, form predictions, regularize with dropout, and choose architectures and training settings.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks
lead: Learn how local filters, shared weights, feature maps, pooling, and skip connections organize image-processing networks.

title: RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs
lead: Follow how shared recurrent state models ordered inputs, then compare LSTM and GRU gates and state outputs.

title: Sequence-to-Sequence and Encoder–Decoder Models
lead: Understand how ordered inputs map to outputs, compare sequence-task types, and trace the encoder–context–decoder flow.

title: Autoencoders and Learned Representations
lead: Autoencoders compress an input into a code and learn to reconstruct it, including from a corrupted view.

title: GANs: Objective, Training, and Failure Modes
lead: Understand how an implicit generator learns through an adversarial discriminator, why the objectives differ, and where training can fail.

title: GAN Architectures, Conditional Generation, and Extensions
lead: How GAN designs change when generation must preserve image structure, encode useful variation, follow a condition, or translate between domains.

title: Time Series Analysis and Forecasting
lead: A forecast is only as trustworthy as its time ordering, information boundary, and error measure. This guide moves from recognizing temporal structure to building and evaluating leakage-safe forecasts.

title: Explainable AI: Questions, Methods, and Presentation
lead: Choose an explanation by starting with the human question, then match its scope, model assumptions, and presentation to the person who must use it.

title: Integrated Gradients, SHAP, and Grad-CAM
lead: Choose the scalar output and reference first; then read input, hidden-unit, coalition, or spatial attributions with their assumptions and limits.

title: Imbalanced Data: Metrics and Resampling
lead: Rare events can be easy to miss even when a classifier is correct on most rows. This guide connects the shape and causes of imbalance to class-aware metrics, sampling choices, threshold decisions, and leakage-safe evaluation.

title: Data Augmentation for Images and Text
lead: Augmentation creates varied training examples only when their task-relevant meaning and labels stay valid; this guide connects text strategies to a controlled image-classification assignment.

title: Machine Translation: Rule-Based and Statistical Methods
lead: Classical machine translation must preserve a message while changing its word order and form. This page follows the shift from hand-written linguistic rules to phrase-based statistical translation.

title: Neural Machine Translation, Attention, and Transformers
lead: Neural machine translation learns one sequence-to-sequence model, then uses attention to connect target predictions to source information. The Transformer replaces recurrence with masked and unmasked attention, while subword units help keep rare words representable.

title: Translation Decoding, Multilingual Models, and Evaluation
lead: Translation systems must search through possible outputs, share evidence across languages, and be evaluated for meaning as well as surface overlap.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Vision
lead: Learn how vision models manufacture training targets from images, shape contrastive or masked objectives, and test whether the retained representation transfers.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Text
lead: Follow how text objectives evolve from static word statistics to contextual prediction, replacement detection, and sequence denoising.

title: Reinforcement Learning: MDPs, Values, and Exploration
lead: Follow how actions, delayed rewards, values, and exploration fit together in a finite Markov decision process.

title: Q-Learning and Temporal-Difference Updates
lead: Learn how Q-values are updated from sampled transitions, how terminal and stochastic cases change the target, and when convergence claims apply.

title: AWS Companion: AI and Generative AI Foundations
lead: An optional companion survey of AI, machine learning, generative AI, and foundation models. It connects the data and workflow choices behind predictions to the tasks and limits of generated output.

title: AWS Companion: Prompt Engineering and Foundation Models
lead: Optional companion reading on prompt design, foundation-model selection and evaluation, generation controls, retrieval, and adaptation. This material is separate from the assumed CS4681 exam route.

title: AWS Companion: Responsible AI, Security, Governance, and Compliance
lead: An optional companion on responsible AI and security boundaries in the 2025 AWS course material; outside the assumed CS4681 exam route.

title: AWS Companion: Application Design and Certification Map
lead: Optional AWS course reading on generative-AI application design and a historical 2025 certification map; outside the assumed CS4681 exam route.
